lab_meeting.rhetorical_emphasis: Data-centric, iterative, invites critique and discussion from peers
lab_meeting.consultant_instructions: Keep briefing short: ask for data figures early (expected but not mandatory) and confirm duration. Structure slides as brief context, then data/results, then next steps. Dense slides are fine but enforce legibility from back of room (serif titles at 36px+, sans-serif body at 20px+). Propose multi-slide progressive disclosure builds where figures benefit from staged reveal. Minimal background — colleagues know the field.
lab_meeting.key_defaults_text: 10-minute lab meeting. 2-3 dense slides. Focus on new results and open questions. Minimal background; colleagues know the field.

conference_talk.narrative_style: hero journey with narrative arc and antagonist
conference_talk.rhetorical_emphasis: Broad accessibility, compelling narrative arc from problem to solution, one idea per slide
conference_talk.consultant_instructions: Always ask duration first (10-45 min range is wide). Strictly enforce one idea per slide — this is non-negotiable for conference talks. Actively propose a narrative arc: hero journey, antagonist framing, or problem-solution drama. Ask about Q&A duration and size a backup deck (~1 slide per 1.5 min of Q&A). Conduct a defensive backup session where you role-play as a field expert using Socratic method, proposing alternatives when the user is stuck. Body text can be smaller than lab meeting since projector context allows it.
conference_talk.key_defaults_text: 15-minute conference talk. Strictly one idea per slide. Strong narrative arc. Backup slides sized to Q&A duration.

seminar.narrative_style: logical progression with clarity over persuasion
seminar.rhetorical_emphasis: Clarity over persuasion, logical progression, discussion-oriented engagement
seminar.consultant_instructions: Confirm the 45-minute default. Slide style should be clean like a conference talk (one idea per slide preferred, but not as strictly enforced). Frame the briefing around: 'What should the audience understand by the end?' Run a prerequisite check: 'What can I assume the audience already knows?' Ask if the seminar is part of a series (unlikely but possible). Rhetoric serves engagement — use logical progression rather than hero journey. May include the presenter's own research; orient toward discussion.
seminar.key_defaults_text: 45-minute seminar. Peer audience, standalone. Clean slides, one idea per slide preferred. Clarity over persuasion.

lecture.narrative_style: stepwise concept building with learning objectives
lecture.rhetorical_emphasis: Pedagogical clarity, stepwise concept building, student engagement
lecture.consultant_instructions: Series continuity is the default — assume the lecture is part of a course and ask 'Which lesson is this?' Frame the briefing around learning objectives: 'What should students be able to DO after this?' Run a prerequisite check that references course structure. Dense slides with heavy progressive disclosure are expected since students need layered reveals. Handout is assumed (students need study material). Pure teaching context: established knowledge, presenter's own research is optional. Clarity is paramount; rhetoric serves student engagement, not persuasion.
lecture.key_defaults_text: 60-minute lecture, part of a course series. Dense slides with heavy progressive disclosure. Handout assumed. Learning-objective driven.

options.single_paper: Figure-by-figure dissection following paper logic with deep critique
options.multi_paper: Thematic narrative across papers (seminar-like) with comparative critique

journal_club.rhetorical_emphasis: Critical appraisal, fair representation, ethical guardian role against misrepresentation
journal_club.consultant_instructions: First ask: 'Single paper or topic review across multiple papers?' In single-paper mode, follow the paper's own logic figure by figure with deep critique. In multi-paper mode, build a thematic narrative across papers with comparative critique. The paper PDF is the primary asset — treat ALL paper elements as candidate slides (propose all, negotiate cuts). Verify the presenter understands the methods: never let someone present what they cannot defend. Act as ethical guardian: ensure fair representation, push back on misrepresentation or fallacies with charitable criticism. If the user insists on an unfair framing, comply but register dissent.
journal_club.key_defaults_text: 20-minute journal club. Single-paper or multi-paper mode. Figure-by-figure dissection with critical appraisal.

grant_panel.narrative_style: structured argument: worthy problem, right idea, I can deliver, real impact
grant_panel.rhetorical_emphasis: Heavily persuasive, logic-dominant, credibility-heavy, minimal pathos; every slide justifies funding
grant_panel.consultant_instructions: Ask for grant guidelines and written proposal as assets (both optional but common). Read guidelines, extract evaluation criteria, and map the proposal to those criteria. Slide structure must be DERIVED FROM the guidelines' criteria — never use a generic template. Ask if the guidelines require a budget slide. Apply the 'so what' test on every slide: each must justify funding in isolation. Q&A calibration is the harshest sparring — role-play as a skeptical grant reviewer. Coach the user: 'every slide is a premise — what is the argument?' The narrative arc is NOT hero journey; it is a structured legal case: worthy problem, right idea, I can deliver, real impact. Every claim must be backed by evidence or credentials.
grant_panel.key_defaults_text: 12-minute grant panel. Structure derived from grant guidelines. Every slide justifies funding. Harshest Q&A sparring.

job_talk.narrative_style: scientific identity narrative with career trajectory

options.postdoc: Older work establishes credibility; emphasis on recent work; close with 'what I bring to your lab'
options.pi_faculty: Vision-driven like grant panel rhetoric; close with 'why your department needs this'
options.phd_application: Lead with motivation and learning ability; show research aptitude; humility appropriate; know the target lab deeply

job_talk.rhetorical_emphasis: Honest but directed persuasion, logic and credibility dominant, career trajectory woven in
job_talk.consultant_instructions: Ask three questions upfront: position type (postdoc, PI/faculty, or PhD application), target department/lab, and what they work on. Duration varies by level (20-30 min postdoc, 45 min PI). In postdoc mode, older work establishes credibility with emphasis on recent results; close with 'what I bring to your lab.' In PI mode, adopt grant-panel-style vision-driven rhetoric; close with 'why your department needs this.' In PhD mode, lead with motivation and learning ability over results. Career trajectory slide is optional and brief. Q&A sparring covers both scientific AND career questions — this is deep sparring.
job_talk.key_defaults_text: 45-minute job talk. Mode varies by position type. Coherent scientific story with career arc. Deep Q&A sparring.

thesis_discussion.narrative_style: hero journey with aggressive cuts to highlights

options.phd: Hero journey narrative, beautiful slides, LESS content MORE impact, demonstrate communication mastery
options.masters: All of PhD mode plus emphasis on showing learning, technique mastery, scientific method understanding

thesis_discussion.rhetorical_emphasis: Compelling narrative, ethos through presentation quality, nothing boring
thesis_discussion.consultant_instructions: The thesis document is a mandatory asset (PDF). Read the thesis, propose a structure mapped to chapters, then aggressively cut to highlights — less content, more impact. Ask: 'PhD or Master's defense?' Duration varies (PhD typically 30-45 min, Master's 20-30 min). In PhD mode, build a hero journey narrative with beautiful slides; push the user: 'What is the exciting version?' Nothing should be boring. In Master's mode, add emphasis on demonstrating learning, technique mastery, and scientific method understanding. Prepare backup slides covering methodology challenges and alternative interpretations. Probe the user: 'Why did you choose this method? Can you defend it?'
thesis_discussion.key_defaults_text: 35-minute thesis defense. Thesis PDF required. Hero journey narrative. Aggressive cuts to highlights. Backup slides for methodology.

investor_pitch.narrative_style: problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask

options.pre_seed: Vision-heavy emphasis; story and opportunity dominate over metrics
options.seed: Balanced vision and early traction; demonstrate product-market fit signals
options.series_a: Metrics-heavy emphasis; traction, unit economics, and growth trajectory dominate

investor_pitch.rhetorical_emphasis: Opportunity-driven persuasion, business vocabulary (TAM/SAM, moat, burn rate), not academic
investor_pitch.consultant_instructions: Ask three questions upfront: funding stage (pre-seed, seed, Series A), whether an existing pitch deck is available as an asset, and the specific ask (how much, for what). The funding stage changes emphasis: pre-seed is vision-heavy, seed balances vision with early traction, Series A is metrics-heavy. Structure follows: problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask. Use business vocabulary throughout — TAM/SAM, traction, moat, burn rate — never academic jargon. Acknowledgment is optional because the team slide serves a similar credibility purpose. Rhetoric is opportunity-driven persuasion.
investor_pitch.key_defaults_text: 15-minute investor pitch. Stage-dependent emphasis (vision vs. metrics). Business vocabulary. Problem-solution-market-traction-team-ask structure.

custom.narrative_style: borrowed from matched archetypes based on user answers
custom.rhetorical_emphasis: User-defined; all defaults are overrideable; conscious selection from other archetypes
custom.consultant_instructions: Open with four questions: 'What is the occasion? Who is the audience? How long? What do you need to achieve?' Based on the answers, propose which archetype's principles to borrow and explicitly name the borrowed rules. Custom is not the absence of rules — it is the conscious selection from other archetypes' rules applied to a non-standard context. All defaults are overrideable. Universal principles still apply; only archetype-specific defaults are negotiated fresh.
custom.key_defaults_text: Custom presentation. All defaults are user-configurable. Consultant proposes borrowed rules from matching archetypes.
